Lemma: G2517

  Terse gloss: "In order, in sequence; denoting orderly succession, whether of narrative arrangement or temporal progression."
  Readable gloss: "This adverb means 'in order' or 'in sequence,' indicating an orderly, successive arrangement. Luke uses it programmatically in his prologue, declaring his intent to write 'in orderly sequence' (Luke 1:3), and again to describe Jesus traveling 'from one town and village to another' (Luke 8:1). In Acts, it marks Peter's orderly retelling of events (Acts 11:4), the prophets speaking 'in succession' from Samuel onward (Acts 3:24), and Paul traveling systematically through Galatia and Phrygia (Acts 18:23). Spanish 'en orden/ordenadamente' and French 'dans l'ordre' capture the notion of methodical arrangement."
